decisions.reason: A piqué upholstery fabric close to the core offer with its own web page costs little to keep in the collection, and one year of results is too little to judge its value, so the option stays open.
The bouclé-effect sheer is only mentioned on the website, but keeping a collection fabric made by production partners is cheap while its demand is still uncertain.
A flame-retardant jacquard serves contract and hospitality projects with long specification cycles, so its value will only show over time and holding it costs little.
The double-face wool blend extends the established offer and fits the move toward renewable materials, so the firm keeps it until clearer sales evidence arrives.
The wool bouclé leno is an early-stage option with low carrying costs and fits the sustainability direction, so it is kept despite having only a brief mention online.
